name: Synthetic Short Stock
summary: Short call + long put at the same strike and expiry replicates 100 short shares without borrowing stock; unlimited upside risk and the single most dangerous structure in this family.

legs.strike_rule: ATM: strike nearest spot, call delta 0.45-0.55

max_profit: (strike x 100) - net_debit if the underlying goes to zero
max_loss: UNDEFINED (unlimited): the short call has no upside cap. A single halt-and-reopen gap of +100% on a $60 stock is a $6,000 loss per contract.

greeks.theta: ~0 net; residual is the carry/borrow term

when_to_use: Historically used when the underlying is hard-to-borrow or impossible to short: the options market prices the borrow cost into the combo, so the synthetic is available when the shares are not. There is no volatility use case (vega is zero).
entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: the short call is uncovered. Requires Level 4 approval, which an Alpaca Level 3 account does not have. Include in the bank for completeness only; the order router must reject this slug outright rather than attempting it.
Additional hard block for an automated system regardless of level: max loss is unbounded and cannot be sized safely against a $50k account. Recommended permanent denylist entry.

If ever run at Level 4: hard notional cap of 10% of equity ($5,000), and a mandatory protective long call at strike x 1.15 converting it into a defined-risk structure (which is then a synthetic short with a cap, not this strategy).

Borrow-cost check: do not open if (combo credit - (spot - strike)) implies an annualised borrow rate above 15%; above that the shares are hard-to-borrow for a reason (squeeze risk) and the synthetic inherits it.
management_rules: Treat as a 100-share short: close at +10% of notional profit or -7% notional loss.
Hard stop is unconditional and must be a resting order, not a monitored condition, because the loss is unbounded and gaps are the failure mode.
If the short call's extrinsic value drops below 1.25x any declared dividend before its ex-date, close the short call that session (see assignment_risk).
Do not average down. Ever. There is no defined loss to average into.
exit_rules: MANDATORY ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short call no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
If the short call is ITM (spot > strike) at any time on expiration day, close it by 14:00 ET.
Close the short call by 15:00 ET the session BEFORE any ex-dividend date if call_extrinsic = call_mid - max(0, spot - strike) < 1.25 x declared_dividend.
Close the entire structure if the underlying is halted and reopens more than 10% higher, at the first available print.
assignment_risk: EXTREME. The short call is subject to early assignment for dividend capture: any ITM call whose remaining extrinsic value is less than the upcoming dividend will be exercised the day before the ex-date. Assignment creates a short stock position of 100 shares, which in a cash-or-limited-margin context is a violation and in a margin account incurs borrow fees and buy-in risk. American style, share settled — there is no cash-settlement escape hatch on equities and ETFs.
buying_power: Reg T naked short call: greater of (20% of underlying value - OTM amount + premium) and (10% of underlying value + premium). Typically $2,000-$3,000 per contract on a $100 name, and it can be called for more intraday.
liquidity_needs: Package bid-ask <= 2% of strike; OI >= 1,000 per leg. Thin names are exactly the hard-to-borrow ones where this is tempting and where the gap risk is worst.
common_mistakes: Using it to short a squeeze candidate because the shares are unborrowable — the borrow cost is embedded in the combo price and the squeeze risk is undiminished. Also assuming the long put 'covers' the short call: it does not, the put is below the call's risk, not above it.
zero_dte_notes: Never. Unbounded risk with no time for a stop to work.
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
